import pytest
    import numpy as np
    from pandas.core.arrays import NumpyExtensionArray

    @pytest.mark.parametrize(
        "dtype",
        [
            np.bool_,
            np.uint8,
            np.uint16,
            np.uint32,
            np.uint64,
            np.int8,
            np.int16,
            np.int32,
            np.int64,
        ],
    )
    def test_take_assigns_floating_point_dtype(dtype):
        # GH#62448.
        if dtype == np.bool_:
            array = NumpyExtensionArray(np.array([False, True, False], dtype=dtype))
            expected = np.dtype(object)
        else:
            array = NumpyExtensionArray(np.array([1, 2, 3], dtype=dtype))
            expected = np.float64
    
        # Ensure fill_value is of expected dtype when converted
        fill_value = np.nan if expected == np.float64 else np.array([None], dtype=object)[0]

        result = array.take([-1], allow_fill=True, fill_value=fill_value)
        assert result.dtype == expected

import pytest
    import numpy as np
    from pandas.core.arrays import NumpyExtensionArray

    @pytest.mark.parametrize(
        "dtype",
        [
            np.bool_,
            np.uint8,
            np.uint16,
            np.uint32,
            np.uint64,
            np.int8,
            np.int16,
            np.int32,
            np.int64,
        ],
    )
    def test_take_assigns_floating_point_dtype(dtype):
        # GH#62448.
        if dtype == np.bool_:
            array = NumpyExtensionArray(np.array([False, True, False], dtype=dtype))
            expected = np.dtype(object)
        else:
            array = NumpyExtensionArray(np.array([1, 2, 3], dtype=dtype))
            expected = np.float64
    
        # Use fill_value as np.nan to induce a floating-point result
        result = array.take([-1], allow_fill=True, fill_value=np.nan)
        
        # Comparing the dtype of the result to the expected dtype
        assert result.dtype == expected
